title: Length Word Problems
intro: Use a consistent scale to explain two changes in a length.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Join the two ribbon lengths in a drawing, then mark the part cut off. Label the remaining length in the same unit.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

The green and orange lengths meet end to end. The dashed part is cut off and is not part of the remaining length. The drawing keeps the same scale in each row; it is not a ruler and is not printed at actual size.

7 + 5 = 12

The joined ribbon is 12 cm long.

12 − 3 = 9

The remaining ribbon is 9 cm long.

Ask your student

Which length is the whole before the cut?

If your student needs help

If the diagram and equation disagree, rebuild the sequence of joining and cutting together.
